status_meaning: Evidence dispositions, not user acceptance or completion percentages. Root-scoped IDs remain distinct.
reference_resolution: repository_source.path is relative to repository root at candidate. included_evidence.path is relative to this dated directory. omitted_local_artifact.catalog_id resolves to omitted-artifacts.json entries, not to an available file. selector is a source line or original JSON check name, not a completion claim.

criteria.text: A new identity can be a Falcon-1024 account that signs payments with pqsig.
criteria.limits: Actual TypeScript default Falcon payment confirmed and both endpoints recover through indexer; not all-six Falcon client qualification.

criteria.text: Importing a 25-word phrase without naming a scheme recovers the classical Ed25519 account.
criteria.limits: Default Ed25519 import and Falcon opt-in paths covered by source unit tests.

criteria.text: Falcon identity does not make X25519 key exchange quantum-safe.
criteria.limits: Falcon payment signing does not replace envelope key agreement; algorithm/security boundary, not a probabilistic security proof.

criteria.text: Only the sender and recipient can read a message.
criteria.limits: Successful sender/recipient opens plus wrong-recipient negative cases; finite tests do not prove universal confidentiality.

criteria.text: If someone tampers with the bytes, decryption fails closed and never leaks plaintext.
criteria.limits: Authenticated payload/tag tamper cases reject; v1 header binding is weaker than v2 and broad all-byte promise needs mode-specific treatment.

criteria.text: When we both have a post-quantum key, a message stays private even if X25519 is later broken, and a person without that key still gets a classical message.
criteria.limits: Low-level hybrid mesh passes; automatic high-level PQ selection/classical fallback is not integrated.

criteria.text: Addresses, timing, and on-chain activity stay public. The protocol does not claim otherwise.
criteria.limits: Current protocol/security docs disclose public addresses, timing and activity; no anonymity claim.

criteria.text: The protocol does not provide forward secrecy.
criteria.limits: Protocol docs correctly disclaim forward secrecy; misleading developer test/demo labels remain.

criteria.text: I can add a pre-shared key so the message key does not rest on X25519 alone.
criteria.limits: Cross-language Extra lock envelopes require correct PSK in targeted negative cases; no complete state-machine acceptance claim.

criteria.text: I can qualify all six libraries before a release without publishing packages.
criteria.limits: All six local package/consumer qualification lanes plus Swift Linux are checked; no remote registry publication or old Apple/Android qualification.

criteria.text: I can see exactly which release evidence is missing and which checks ran against the candidate commit.
criteria.limits: Local evidence records exact candidate, toolchains, exits, artifacts, known missing coverage and failures; it is not hosted/release authorization.

criteria.text: I can find the protocol and the TypeScript, Swift, Python, Rust, Kotlin, and Go libraries in one AlgoChat repository.
criteria.limits: Single checkout contains canonical protocol and all six language roots.

criteria.text: The libraries speak envelope versions 0x01 and 0x02, and protocols 0x01, 0x02, 0x04, and 0x05. Identifier 0x03 is unassigned. The earlier note that postponed post-quantum envelopes is historical.
criteria.limits: Current cross-language reads cover v1/v2 classical/PSK and hybrid protocols04/05; no unassigned03 writer path.

criteria.text: A message is an encrypted note on an Algorand payment. There is no mailbox or extra router.
criteria.limits: Direct payment notes confirmed on LocalNet, including separate high-level TypeScript Falcon send/read; no router contract involved.

criteria.sentence: My 25-word recovery phrase is all I need to get my chat identity back.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/keys.md:15
criteria.assessment: Identity reconstruction tested for explicit schemes. A default Falcon phrase imported without scheme produces an Ed25519 address, so the words alone do not select original identity; PSK/session state recovery is separate.

criteria.sentence: Importing a phrase I already use elsewhere gives me the same address my wallet shows.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/keys.md:16
criteria.assessment: Ed25519 import/address and algosdk account equivalence exercised locally; no external wallet UI tested.

criteria.sentence: The same words give me the same encryption key whichever signature scheme I pick.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/keys.md:17
criteria.assessment: Same mnemonic produces identical X25519 keys across Ed25519/Falcon, with distinct addresses.

criteria.sentence: A brand-new account signs with a post-quantum signature unless I ask otherwise.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/keys.md:18
criteria.assessment: Default Falcon account creation exercised. Explicit Ed25519 import exercised; signer transaction tests use stubs.

criteria.sentence: I can publish my encryption key so anyone can start writing to me.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/keys.md:19
criteria.assessment: Signed announcement/payment construction exercised with stubbed algod; no high-level fresh on-chain publish/discover acceptance in this TS lane.

criteria.sentence: I can find someone's encryption key from their address alone, without asking them for it.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/keys.md:20
criteria.assessment: Address-based discovery/pagination exercised with stub indexers. Not an unrestricted live network discovery proof.

criteria.sentence: I am told whether that key is proven to belong to the address or only trusted on first use.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/keys.md:21
criteria.assessment: Verified/TOFU metadata positive and negative cases exercised; concrete service exposes discoverPublicKeyWithMetadata.

criteria.sentence: A forged key announcement is never accepted, not even as an unverified key.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/keys.md:22
criteria.assessment: Malformed/wrong-signer/invalid-signature announcements rejected in finite local fixtures.

criteria.sentence: I can show a short fingerprint so two people can compare keys out of band.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/keys.md:23
criteria.assessment: Fingerprint format/determinism/distinction tested. Actual person-to-person comparison untested.

criteria.sentence: My private keys never leave my process; everything is signed where I run it.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/keys.md:24
criteria.assessment: Ed25519/Falcon local signing and outgoing signed transaction exercised with stubbed transport. No exhaustive private-key exfiltration instrumentation/security audit.

criteria.sentence: When I keep keys on disk they are encrypted with my password and readable only by my user.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/keys.md:25
criteria.assessment: Direct built FileKeyStorage implementation passes password/tamper/final permissions checks under temp directory override. It is absent from root package exports; recommended /node subpath throws ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED. No transient write-permission/race proof.

criteria.sentence: Only the sender and the recipient can read what a message says.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/private.md:15
criteria.assessment: Sender/recipient/wrong-key cases pass; six-language interoperability is separate parent evidence. Finite tests do not establish exclusive readability against all attackers.

criteria.sentence: A tampered message fails to open instead of showing altered or partial text.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/private.md:16
criteria.assessment: Recorded standard/PSK/PQ corruption cases fail closed without plaintext. Complete adversarial input space untested.

criteria.sentence: Changing any header byte, the version included, makes the message fail to open.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/private.md:17
criteria.assessment: Version2 full-header binding exercised; legacy version1 remains readable and lacks full-header authentication. The unconditional criterion is not met by every supported version.

criteria.sentence: I am told plainly what is not protected: who talks to whom, when, and my whole history if a key or phrase leaks.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/private.md:18
criteria.assessment: Documentation explicitly states public metadata/no forward secrecy and mode-specific recovery limits. No usability comprehension test performed.

criteria.sentence: I can add a pre-shared key so an attacker needs it as well as the key exchange to read my messages.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/private.md:19
criteria.assessment: PSK positive and missing/wrong-key failures exercised. Classical optional PSK and counter-bearing PSK are distinct APIs.

criteria.sentence: I can hand that key to the other person with one QR scan.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/private.md:20
criteria.assessment: Exchange URI roundtrip exercised; QR encoding/camera scan/device exchange not part of library and not tested.

criteria.sentence: A replayed pre-shared-key message is rejected.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/private.md:21
criteria.assessment: Explicit helper rejects recorded duplicate when caller validates/persists state. Low-level decrypt does not itself enforce replay; atomic concurrent check/record and restart persistence not established. Negative/fractional counters accepted; send counter overflows wire range.

criteria.sentence: Messages written before a protocol upgrade stay readable after it.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/private.md:22
criteria.assessment: Legacy version1 decryption and frozen compatibility fixtures pass85 checks. This does not cover every historical app/storage migration.

criteria.sentence: The cryptography comes from audited libraries rather than home-grown primitives.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/private.md:23
criteria.assessment: No independent audit evidence for the complete shipped PQ/signature dependency set or AlgoChat integration. Algorithm standardization is not audit acceptance.

criteria.sentence: I can send an encrypted message to any Algorand address with one call once I have their key.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/send.md:15
criteria.assessment: One-call standard send signs/submits with stubbed algod using valid accounts. High-level automatic PQ/PSK negotiation and arbitrary live recipients are unproven.

criteria.sentence: A reply carries a pointer to the message it answers and a short preview of it.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/send.md:16
criteria.assessment: Actual service reply path tested with string txid plus preview. README sends ReplyContext object as fifth argument, yielding TS2554 expected6-7 got5; documented example is broken.

criteria.sentence: I choose whether a send waits for confirmation, for the indexer, or for neither.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/send.md:17
criteria.assessment: Options implemented; default non-wait sends exercised. No targeted confirmation/indexer success/timeout path tests found or executed in native suite.

criteria.sentence: A message too big for one payment note is refused before anything is signed or paid for.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/send.md:18
criteria.assessment: Outgoing one-byte oversize limits and byte-count Unicode overflow exercised before send/sign. Decoders accept oversize inbound objects; authenticated PQ4097 decrypt succeeds.

criteria.sentence: I can rebuild a conversation, both sides of it, from the chain alone with nothing stored locally.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/send.md:19
criteria.assessment: Classical sender/recipient crypto recovery tested. Full high-level chain reconstruction without cache not exercised in this TS lane; PSK secret/replay state and PQ sessions are additional recovery requirements.

criteria.sentence: I can read my own sent messages back, not only the ones sent to me.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/send.md:20
criteria.assessment: Sender opens recorded notes for each mode using its required keys; no high-level complete sent-history acceptance asserted.

criteria.sentence: Messages come back in the order they happened.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/send.md:21
criteria.assessment: Runtime reproducer uses one round/one timestamp with offsets5 then1: concrete AlgorandService reorders correctly, exported MessageIndexer and abstract MessageIndexer return offset5 before1, and Conversation retains reversed insertion order. Ledger ordering is inconsistent.

criteria.sentence: A note I cannot decrypt is skipped instead of breaking the whole conversation.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/send.md:22
criteria.assessment: Actual fetch/decrypt with a stub indexer containing valid sent, tampered received, valid received notes passed for concrete service, exported MessageIndexer and abstract MessageIndexer on Node18. Bad note skipped, both good directions recovered; no live indexer/network proof.

criteria.sentence: I can queue messages while offline and have them go out when I am back online.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/send.md:23
criteria.assessment: Temp runtime harness exercises offline queue and reconnect processing with service stub; actual network loss/reconnect and background timers not established.

criteria.sentence: A message that keeps failing stops retrying after a bounded number of attempts, and I am told.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/send.md:24
criteria.assessment: Native queue transitions and temp SyncManager stub fail exactly3 attempts then notify permanent failure.

criteria.sentence: The queue survives a restart when I give it durable storage.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/send.md:25
criteria.assessment: Native persistence test uses in-memory storage. Temp file backend saves/loads across new instances, not killed process/crash. File backend has no supported package export and explicit save is required.

criteria.sentence: A message sent from this library reads the same in every other AlgoChat implementation, and theirs read the same here.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/send.md:26
criteria.assessment: TS85-check frozen corpus passes; parent has six-language mesh evidence. Complete high-level client/platform parity is absent and finite cross-language cases do not prove every possible message.

criteria.sentence: A change to the bytes on the wire is caught as a protocol change, not waved through as a test update.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/send.md:27
criteria.assessment: Frozen verifier85 checks ran locally; deterministic-regeneration tripwire is not in active qualification and was not rerun in this lane. Review policy governs fixture changes.

criteria.sentence: I can test everything my app does with AlgoChat without a live network or credentials.
criteria.criterion: ts/hi/send.md:28
criteria.assessment: 270 unique source tests execute offline plus28 runtime checks with stubs. FileKeyStorage/SyncManager/high-level wait/indexer acceptance not completely covered natively; no all-app-behavior proof.

criteria.criterion: I can share a pre-shared key with a contact as a single link.
criteria.limits: URI encode/parse/import/send tested on LocalNet.

criteria.criterion: A malformed link is refused rather than half imported.
criteria.limits: Invalid scheme, missing fields and wrong key length cases rejected; not exhaustive arbitrary-input fuzzing.

criteria.criterion: Reading a message with a PSK contact takes both the pre-shared key and our account keys.
criteria.limits: Wrong PSK/private key and third-party paths reject; successful correct-peer LocalNet path also exercised.

criteria.criterion: Every PSK message uses its own key derived from the shared one.
criteria.limits: Ordinary derivation vectors pass, but send counter max wraps to0, reusing the position-key input. Unique-per-message goal is not met over counter exhaustion.

criteria.criterion: A PSK message that someone copies into a new transaction is refused as a replay.
criteria.limits: Counter duplicate rejection works, but transaction identity is not distinguished: legitimate same-transaction reopening is rejected. Concurrent high-level PSK receive atomicity not claimed.

criteria.criterion: A message whose counter is far outside what I expect from that contact is refused.
criteria.limits: Bounded +/-200 window exercised. UInt32 API excludes fractional/negative values by type; no dynamic JavaScript-style number conversion path.

criteria.criterion: A message that fails to decrypt never uses up a counter.
criteria.limits: Actual public indexer path returns0 for auth-flipped note then1 for valid same-counter note, proving this tested failed decrypt did not burn counter.

criteria.criterion: Reading the same transaction again, as when I reopen a conversation, is never treated as a replay.
criteria.limits: Same transaction first read1, second read0, new manager over stored state0. Deterministically violates reopening criterion.

criteria.criterion: PSK messaging is optional, and standard messages keep working alongside it.
criteria.limits: Standard/PSK coexistence and optional PSK paths exercised.

criteria.criterion: My PSK contacts and their counters survive a restart.
criteria.limits: New manager reads retained contact/counter state from file, but separate OS process/crash-durability test not run. Plain JSON secret/state does not provide encryption at rest; reimporting via addContact initializes state if manager cache is empty.

criteria.criterion: I can send a text message to any Algorand address, and only that person and I can read it.
criteria.limits: Standard local-chain send/receive, sender readback and wrong/third-party keys exercised; this is not independent cryptographic assurance.

criteria.criterion: Anyone watching the chain can see that we talked, when, and roughly how much, but never what was said.
criteria.limits: Local-chain metadata and ciphertext plus wrong-key rejection support the boundary; does not establish an absolute never-content assurance or side-channel audit.

criteria.criterion: I can read my own sent messages again from the chain, on any device that holds my account.
criteria.limits: Sender readback exercised; cross-device account restoration not an end-to-end acceptance test, and PSK history additionally requires PSK/state. Reopening an already seen PSK tx fails (PSK-4.c).

criteria.criterion: A message too big for one transaction is refused before anything is paid for.
criteria.limits: Outbound encryption/transaction construction rejects oversize before sending. Standalone inbound parser/PQ size gaps are separate recorded defects.

criteria.criterion: I choose whether sending returns as soon as the message is submitted, once it is confirmed, or once it can be read back.
criteria.limits: Option models and successful confirmation/indexer LocalNet flows exercised; three timing/failure semantics not independently fault-injected.

criteria.criterion: Even when I do not wait, I get the message back straight away to show in my own view.
criteria.limits: Returned message used in successful sends; no strict immediate-return timing assertion or submission-failure acceptance test.

criteria.criterion: I can open a conversation with someone and refresh it without downloading everything again.
criteria.limits: Incremental refresh and de-duplication exercised; history pagination/PSK repeat reads have separate gaps.

criteria.criterion: I can page back through older history when I want it.
criteria.limits: loadOlder is implemented, but no exact backward-conversation-pagination acceptance test identified/executed. Key-discovery pagination tests do not establish this criterion.

criteria.criterion: Messages I have already cached are still there when I am offline.
criteria.limits: Cache storage/retrieval tested; actual network-offline cached conversation UX and process restart not exercised. Default optional cache is not a durable store.

criteria.criterion: I can reply to a specific message, and the other side sees what I was replying to.
criteria.limits: Reply metadata/preview roundtrip and on-chain context preserved in tested standard/PSK cases.

criteria.criterion: A message written by any AlgoChat implementation can be read by this one, and the other way round.
criteria.limits: Six-language valid-note mesh and LocalNet matrix support interoperable tested paths. Parser minimum/maximum and counter-state differences prevent full edge-case parity; automatic high-level PQ not integrated.

criteria.criterion: When I am offline, a message I write waits in a queue and goes out later.
criteria.limits: Queue creation, persistence and online-state behavior tested. SyncManager tests omit a real chat client; end-to-end offline queue recovery/send not exercised.

criteria.criterion: A queued message is never reported as sent when it was not.
criteria.limits: Failed queue-state persistence tested; no actual blockchain submission-failure/recovery acceptance with SyncManager.

criteria.criterion: Something on the chain that is not a message for me never breaks my conversation list.
criteria.limits: Known nonchat/malformed envelope cases rejected/skipped. No exhaustive/fuzzed conversation-list pollution acceptance run; parser oversize gaps remain.

criteria.criterion: A message costs me the network minimum and nothing more unless I choose to send more.
criteria.limits: Current expected fees 1000/1098/1308 include note-size surcharge above1024, contradicting the unconditional minimum-only sentence. User criterion retained unchanged.

criteria.criterion: My encryption key comes from my Algorand account, so the account is the only thing I have to back up.
criteria.limits: Account-derived classical encryption identity only; does not claim recovery of independently shared PSKs or state.

criteria.criterion: The same account gives the same encryption key on every device and in every AlgoChat implementation.
criteria.limits: Six local implementations and two account pairs; not every supported runtime/platform.

criteria.criterion: I can make myself reachable before anyone has messaged me by publishing my key once.
criteria.limits: Publish-key LocalNet path exercised on the recorded candidate.

criteria.criterion: Someone can find my key on the chain without having to ask me for it.
criteria.limits: Mock pagination plus LocalNet account-key discovery; public networks not exercised.

criteria.criterion: A key I published myself is shown as proven to belong to my address.
criteria.limits: Signed announcement verification, wrong-account and corrupted-signature cases.

criteria.criterion: A key that was only seen in passing is shown as unverified, never as trusted.
criteria.limits: Unsigned/observed classical and PSK keys retain unverified status in tested cases.

criteria.criterion: I can limit how much history is searched when looking for a key.
criteria.limits: Mock search limits/page size/backward-compatible depth exercised.

criteria.criterion: I can compare a short fingerprint of a key with someone out of band.
criteria.limits: Fingerprint format and stability exercised; no human comparison ceremony.

criteria.criterion: On Apple devices my stored encryption key can sit behind Face ID, Touch ID or Optic ID.
criteria.limits: Biometric hardware/UX not locally exercised; tvOS/watchOS memory fallback does not provide this Apple-device storage capability. Generic-password Keychain is not Secure Enclave storage.

criteria.criterion: Everywhere else my stored encryption key is protected by a password I choose.
criteria.limits: Explicit password-file storage tested on macOS and Linux (Linux FileKeyStorage tests executed in isolated container). Other Apple platforms are not exercised; fallback is memory unless durable storage is selected explicitly.

criteria.criterion: A wrong password or a damaged key file fails with an error and never hands back a wrong key.
criteria.limits: Wrong password and a last-byte-corrupted encrypted key file both fail without returning a key on macOS; arbitrary filesystem failure cases not exhaustive.
